SportsTab.title: Manchester United v Bournemouth, Liverpool v Brighton and more: clockwatch – live
SportsTab.text:
Carrick sends on Shea Lacey, mystifyingly ignored after being given a chance against Brighton in the League Cup and scoring a beauty. He replaces Amad, unproductive yet again.

The story today will, of course, be how awful United are and the likelihood they change manager in the next few days. But Bournemouth have been good and everything they aren’t, quick, strong, focused, organised, competent, inventive and so on.

Carrick sends on Zirkzee for Baleba, which makes you wonder why he put Bruno on the bench; there’s no footballing justification for leaving him on there, so if it’s unitive, why not leave him out altogether? Revenge? I guess he probably isn’t getting the chance to wreak any more.

Updated at 11.38 EDT

WHAT A GOAL! Manchester United 0-3 AFC Bournemouth (Evanilson 71)

Adams swings a pass in behind, inside-right channel, and Evanilson is on to it, Lammens racing out but arriving second – perhaps the ball held up in the wind, perhaps he was never getting there. So Evanilson pokes past the keeper on the inside, runs past on the outside and, from outside the box, right-hand side of it, with Maguire lolloping back to cover, swings a stunning finish high into the far side-netting! Bournemouth have won 3-0 at Old Trafford twice in the last three seasons, and they’re poised to do so again – but might make things yet worse for United.

Updated at 11.34 EDT

Liverpool push for a third goal, Gakpo away down the right but failing to find the ma in the middle.

United are, at least, spending some time attacking this half, Martinez shooting wide from distance, but they’re not sustaining attacks not seriously extending Petrovic. At Anfield, Nyoni has replaced Wirtz but is now struggling himself.

Another change from Carrick and again it’s not Bruno, Martinez on for Heaven, who had a shocker. For all the difference it makes, Rayan easing past Dalot and running atMartinez, who steps across him, only to allow his man through on the inside. he has options at the far post too, but opts to shoot, his low effort scuttling just wide.

GOAL! Hull City 1-1 Brentford (Ouattara 63)

A ball swung into the box bumps about, then Igor Thiago finds Ouattara and he taps home from a few yards.

Updated at 11.29 EDT

Change for Bournemouth, Gannon-Doak on for Kluivert.

United are pushing at OT, Mbeumo going down when Adams jumps into him – United want a penalty but they’re never getting that – then, when Yoro finds him, he swings a shot over the bar. So they come again, Dalot lifting over Smith’s foot to go down the line and winning a corner, driven into Petrovic’s gloves.

Updated at 11.25 EDT

At Anfield, Brighton probe seeking a route back into the game, Yalcouye on for Chema. Oh, and as I type, Wirtz flails a leg at Ayari, fouling with the ball out of reach, lands awkwardly, and gosh, he looks in a lot of pain. He does, though, make a quick recovery, so will, I think, be back on shortly.

GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-2 Newcastle United (Barnes 58)

Pierre Sage is another manager in deep trouble, Newcastle working Dedic into space down the right of the box, with his hard square-pass swept home by Barnes.

Updated at 11.21 EDT

In comms, Gary Neville thinks Tielemans should’ve stayed on with Andrey Santos going off, and it’s hard to argue with that. United need goals, Tielemans can supply them, and Baleba should supply the solidity necessary given the game-state.

“Half-time sacking,” begins Ingo hHrtzke. “That question has come up before – so I’m once more sending a famous example from Germany’s 2nd division, about 26 years ago in December 1999 Toni Schumacher was managing Fortuna Cologne, who had a very colourful chairman at the time: Jean Löring. After a spell of bad results they were trailing 0-2 at home to Mannheim at half time, Löring stormed into the dressing room and shouted: ‘Piss off, you wanker! I never want to see you again.’ (That’s how Schumacher told it in his memoir.) To the press afterwards, he spoke the immortal words: ‘As the club, I had to act.’ Classic.”

A lovely example of l’etat c’est moi, but looking at this United side, 1999 was at least 260 years ago.

I’m not sure what Carrick’s trying to achieve by not bringing Bruno on. United probably won’t come back with him, but without him, it feels impossible.

At Palace, Willock is sent through and finishes well, doing what Rayan tried to but well … only for VAR to show a shoulder offside.

Heaven, having a mare, passes straight to Rayan, who exchanges passes with Kluivert then opens body to find the far corner only to finish too close to Lammens, who saves.

Not all that long ago, in October 2018, Jose Mourinho was about to get sacked with United 2-o down at home to Newcastle. Then they came back, won 3-2, and Mourinho lasted until just before Christmas, wreaking yet further havoc in the meantime.

Goodness me, a ricochet off heaven, dithering from Maguire, and a pass in behind is tucked away by Evanilson … who’s offside. He leaves that for Rayan, and it’s 3-0. United are an absolute debacle.

GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-1 Newcastle United (Osula 48)

Newcastle build down the right and Murphy swings over a brilliant cross, which Osula tucks home at the near post and on the volley.

Updated at 11.13 EDT

At Old Trafford, still no Bruno Fernandes, but Cunha is on for Tielemans. We’re underway again.

“Eamon Dunphy, in his fine diary of a season Only a Game?, broke the substitute’s omertà by revealing that most players who are dropped are delighted when their replacements fail on the pitch,” says Justin Kavanagh. “I’m sure Bruno Fernandes has a warm glow inside as he sits listening to Carrick’s half-time farewell speech team-talk.”

I found that book in the school library aged about 13 and it properly opened my eyes. I was lucky enough to interview Dunphy when making the film Busby, a complete thrill – his book A Strange Kind of Glory is a classic – and only he would have tossed all the interviews he did for it.

Half-time email: “Isak, Wirtz and Barcola seem to be finding their feet at last,” writes Colum Fordham, “and pretty good feet they have too. Liverpool once again pose an attacking threat to any team but the shambolic defence – Van Dijk a shadow of his former self and the erratic Kerkez - threaten to undo the good work. Araujo is definitely one of the most exciting of the new acquisitions for the Reds, his dynamism and strength very much needed. Iraola is managing to keep the dangerous Brighton at bay.”

I’m still not convinced by Wirtz, who flits in and out and doesn’t, I don’t think, make good decisions quickly enough when nuder pressure. But Isak is a class act, and Barcola is excellent when offered space in behind. I don’t love him in tight situations, but if he can improve his, er key actions, i.e. his final pass and finishing, he can be a factor in the Prem.

Looking again at the second Bournemouth goal, Yoro, though he slips, also slows down, when all he needed to do was tap back to Lammens. Without that indecision, he’s no chance to slip because the ball’s already gone.

I’d not be shocked if Carrick makes United’s call for them, Kevin Keegan for England-style – or wouldn’t be if there wasn’t cashmoney involved. He surely knows this is too far gone for him to resolve, and he’s clearly hating every second of it.

HALF-TIME: Hull City 1-0 Brentford

McBurnie’s penalty the difference at the KC as Hull continue their fine start to Premier League life.

HALF-TIME: Manchester United 0-2 AFC Bournemouth

Bournemouth have been energetically excellent, United soporifically shambolic.

HALF-TIME: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton & Hove Albion

Liverpool look really good going forward but so do Brighton; neither look much cop at the back.

United make a bit of space and Tielemans squares for Santos, who near-enough misses his kick, then the ref goes to book Maguire for a shove earlier in the piece.

HALF-TIME: Crystal Palace 0-0 Newcastle United

Nothing between the teams at Selhurst.

Updated at 10.59 EDT

Two additional minutes at Old Trafford, three at Anfield. Meantime, Amad chops inside Smith and falls – he wants a penalty, but it’s nothing of the sort.

“This must be the most mediocre Man Utd XI since the late 80s side of Duxbury, Phelan and Blackmore,” writes Brian Broderick. “But if you give Chelsea £100m for Mount and Santos, that’s where you end up. Which is pretty much what Martinez was saying.”

At least those United sides had Robson, Hughes, Whiteside and McGrath, absolute giants all. I said earlier there are some good players in this squad and there are, but they’re devoid of confidence, organisation and moxie.

GOAL! Manchester United 0-2 AFC Bournemouth (Tavernier 41)

Has a manager ever been sacked at half-time before? A ball in behind Yoro should pose no problem but, out of nowhere but also straight out of M16, Yoro slips, Truffert squares, and Tavernier sweeps home. United are awful, while Bournemouth are all over it.

Updated at 10.48 EDT

United try to hit back immediately. First, Tielemans is booked, then Mount, having wandered infield, slides a pass ahead of Mbeumo, inside-left position, and he shoots across goal, but Petrovic tips away. “Down with the City!” choruses the away end.

GOAL! Manchester United 0-1 AFC Bournemouth (Rayan 38)

Loads of players stand offside and come back but Rayan, the furthest left, is alone and on, mooching on to Kluivert’s outswinging cross to guide a sidefooter into the ground and past Lammens at his near post. It’s been coming.

Updated at 10.47 EDT

Back to Old Trafford now, where Heaven launches two-footed into a challenge, and is saved by Evanilson stepping out of the way. He’s booked, but if he’d made contact, it’s a red card; lucky boy.

A poor kick-out from Alisson puts Liverpool in trouble and Brighton win the ball back, working it to Ayari, who bends a low shot around the keeper, not yet back on his line … and hits the base of the post!

Harry Messguire lummoxes past a few challenges, but can’t find a shooting lane, so passes backwards The crowd though, appreciate the intention and might it spur United to do something? They get the ball wide to Amad, who then leaves it behind him and, when he gets it back, plays a poor pass.

“The Seagulls have been a shambles at the back,” reckons Kári Tulinius. “Being 2-0 down is the least they deserve. Nevertheless, when they mount an attack, Liverpool defend in a panic, and I doubt they’ll keep a clean sheet. There’s no way there won’t be more goals in this match.”

I ‘m inclined to agree – Brighton attack well and Liverpool defend chaotically. If the former manage a livener before the latter bag a clincher, this could be a really exciting contest.

United are offering so little in attack – no width, no 1v1 ability, no sharp passing – and when, as I type, a lovely flick behind the standing leg allows Baleba to find Tielemans, Mbeumo checks his run and the attempted through-pass is easily cut out.

Better from United, Yoro into Tielemans, who flicks superbly for Baleba down the right. He’s got Mbeumo in the middle, but roughly 94 defenders blocking the route to him, and Hill does well to slide in and intercept the cross.

A decent ball in from Adams, to which an unsighted Evanilson can’t quite introduce a head. Bournemouth haven’t had that many chances, but they’ve had loads of good situations, whereas United have had none.

GOAL! Hull City 1-0 Brentford (McBurnie 24 pen)

We’re not shown for what it was given, but McBurnie dispatches it with a confident roll, Kelleher diving out of the road.

Updated at 10.33 EDT

United are just so careless with the ball. Lammens catches a cross and tries to set a counter in motion, but his roll-out sells Mbeumo short and instead, Bournemouth counter. Oh and Andre Santos was booked a few minutes for a lunge; the same has since been done by and to Tyler Adams.

It didn’t look great initially ad they’re still too easy to get at, but we can now say that Liverpool have made a decent start under Andoni Iraola. They’ve got into the habit of winning, Isak is scoring, and they’ve loads of attacking options, while Araujo has given them physicality and aggression they lacked not just last season but even the one before when they won the league.

GOAL! Liverpool 2-0 Brighton & Hove Albion (Isak 21)

It’s taken a while, but Alexander Isak is a Liverpool player now. Boscagli makes a mess controlling an Alisson kick, Barcola does really well to rob him, and from there, it’s simple competence, a careful cross into the middle and a composed sidefooted finish. Yasiin Ayari will be feeling very, very poorly, and this could yet get a lot worse.

Updated at 10.26 EDT

Liverpool keep at it, Verbruggen forced to dive full-length to stop a shot directed across him by Gakpo. Meantime, back in Manchester, it’s now a more even game, though Boournemouth know they can pretty much allow Dalot to have the ball in dangerous areas because nothing will happen thereafter – and, as I type, he lashes a hopeful shot miles from anywhere.

GOAL! Liverpool 1-0 Brighton & Hove Albion (Wirtz 17)

That is how much Brighton will regret missing that chance. Araujo does brilliantly down the right – what an acquisition he’s been so far – ruckusing hard to recover possession before crossing low. The ball hits Gross, lands in front of Wirtz, and though he shoots seeking the far corner, a huge deflection off Andres wrongfoots Verbruggen and gives Liverpool the lead.

Updated at 10.22 EDT

Back to OT and it’s slightly better from United, Mbeumo finding space before running into trouble. They are, though, keeping the ball now, with Baleba seemingly settled into the game.

Oh, but here come Brighton! They fight down the right, Gomez in behind and taking a pass from Gross before cutting back for Ayari, 10 yards out … who panels over the bar! What a chance that was, and how might Brighton rue spurning it?

At Anfield, Costinha has replaced Kadioglu, who gives Brighton so much attacking impetus. We’ve barely seen them in the Liverpool half yet, but they’ve done well to survive the opening period … as have United, sort of – so far, their performance is such that to say they’ve done anything well feels ridiculous. And, as I type, a flick off Yoro prevents a cross from arriving at Evanilson.

SportsTab.title: Jokić says booing fans ‘not welcome’ after Nuggets rally from 23 points down to beat Pelicans
SportsTab.text:
Nikola Jokić scored eight of his 35 points in overtime and finished with 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and the short-handed Denver Nuggets rallied from 23 points down to beat the New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 on Saturday night.

Jokić had his 199th career triple-double in the regular season, second to Russell Westbrook, who retired with 209.

Sections of the Nuggets home crowd booed the team when they went into half-time 73-57 down. After the game, Jokić made his displeasure clear.

“We got booed at our first home game, and I think those fans who booed us, they don’t need to come anymore,” Jokić said. “If you guys follow us, you know that we never quit and we’ve come back from much worse situations. So, if they ask me, they are not welcome anymore.”

Jamal Murray scored 42 points and rookie Trevon Brazille had seven of his 17 points in overtime in his home debut for Denver, which took an early lead in overtime. His corner three-pointer with 1:25 left in overtime gave the Nuggets a 133-129 lead.

Denver played without Cam Johnson (ankle) and Alpha Diallo (sprained wrist) and continued to be without Julian Strawther and Spencer Jones.

Trey Murphy III led New Orleans with 26 points, Dejounte Murray had 22 points and Derik Queen and Zion Williamson scored 17 each. The Pelicans have dropped their first three games under first-year coach Jamahl Mosley.

New Orleans shot 65.9% in the first half and led by 23. Denver rallied to cut it to 16, and Jokić and Murray combined to score 22 of the Nuggets’ 32 points in the third quarter but the Pelicans extended the lead to 19 heading into the fourth.

Denver erased the deficit on three-pointers from Murray and Jokić, a reverse dunk from Aaron Gordon, and then had a chance to go ahead with 17 seconds left but Murray made two of three free throws to tie it.

SportsTab.title: Brewers erase four-run deficit to stun Rays and take 2-0 World Series lead
SportsTab.text:
Sal Frelick tied the score with his first home run in three months, Cooper Pratt hit a go-ahead single in the seventh inning and the Milwaukee Brewers stunned the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 on Saturday night for a 2-0 World Series lead by overcoming a four-run deficit for the second time in the postseason.

Tampa Bay, who won the AL pennant by forcing opponents into mistakes, committed one error, made two other misplays that could have been charged as errors and had a runner thrown out at the plate.

Down 4-0 in the first inning, Milwaukee rallied for their seventh comeback win of this postseason. The Brewers also rebounded from a 4-0 deficit to beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 in Game 4 of the NL Championship Series, completing a four-game sweep.

After losing Friday’s opener 3-2, the Rays burst ahead against rookie Logan Henderson but the Brewers started to claw back with two runs in the bottom half against Tampa Bay ace Drew Rasmussen.

David Hamilton cut the deficit to 4-3 with a run-scoring grounder in the fourth and Frelick capped a nine-pitch at-bat against Ian Seymour in the sixth by driving a fastball over the center-field fence.

Frelick had gone 103 plate appearances without a home run since his 11 July drive off Pittsburgh’s Braxton Ashcraft and had not gone deep against a left-handed pitcher since opening day against Tyler Gilbert of the Chicago White Sox. Frelick sped around the bases in 18.72 seconds, half the time of some theatrical trots this postseason.

Screaming fans at the second game of Milwaukee’s first World Series since 1982 were fired up during the seventh-inning stretch, dancing to the Beer Barrel Polka played by Mike Schneider, an accordionist from Clinton, Wisconsin.

Brice Turang doubled against losing pitcher Tyler Wells on the second pitch of the bottom half, advanced on Garrett Mitchell’s flyout to right and scored when Pratt, a 22-year-old who debuted in June, looped a sinker from Kevin Kelly into short right field.

Abner Uribe pitched one and one-third hitless innings for the win.

Jonny DeLuca doubled off Aaron Ashby starting the ninth, then Victor Mesa Jr struck out when he couldn’t check his swing. Pinch-hitter Ben Williamson’s groundout advanced the runner and Yandy Díaz struck out when he couldn’t check his swing on a full-count pitch.

Ashby has three saves in the postseason while not allowing a run.

Milwaukee won their seventh straight game, becoming the fifth team to twice overcome four-run deficits for victories in a single postseason and the first since Philadelphia in 2022.

Game 3 of the matchup between teams seeking their first title is Monday night at Tropicana Field in St Petersburg, Florida, where the Brewers last played in 2023.

Of the 57 previous teams to take 2-0 World Series leads, 46 claimed the championship.

Tampa Bay took a 4-2 lead in the highest-scoring Series first inning since Game 4 in 1993 as the teams combined for seven hits, tying the most in an opening frame.

Still, Milwaukee improved to 13-0 in games started by Henderson, dating to his 2025 debut. He followed Jacob Misiorowski in the Brewers’ rotation, the first time teammates aged 24 or younger started the first two games of the Series since Cincinnati’s Gary Nolan and Ross Grimsley in 1972.

Henderson started on 11 days’ rest and struggled as the Rays fouled off 13 of 35 pitches in the first. He gave up four runs – three earned – in three innings.

Given an extra day of rest, Rasmussen allowed three runs and six hits over three and two-thirds innings in his shortest start since 9 July.

Pratt made his fourth error of the postseason at shortstop, the Brewers’ ninth in 10 games, bouncing his throw past first baseman Jake Bauers on a leadoff grounder by Díaz. Chandler Simpson and Junior Caminero followed with RBI singles, and Liam Hicks hit a two-run homer.

Jackson Chourio and Bauers started the bottom half with singles and first baseman Jonathan Aranda allowed Contreras’ one-out foul pop to bounce out of his mitt near netting in front of the seats.

With Bauers running on a full-count pitch, Contreras bounced an RBI single to the left of second baseman Richie Palacios, who had taken a step toward the base. Mitchell’s two-out single cut the deficit to 4-2.

Hamilton hit an RBI grounder in the fourth that bounced under Aranda’s legs for an error.

Chourio threw out Hicks from left for the final out of the sixth when third base coach Brady Williams waved the slow-footed catcher to try to score from second on Mesa’s single.

SportsTab.title: The WNBA finals are a basketball wonderland – unless you’re part of the Maga machine
SportsTab.text:
When Tyler Perry leading lady Crystal Renee took center stage at State Farm Arena to sing the national anthem before the Atlanta Dream’s WNBA finals clash with the Golden State Valkyries on Saturday afternoon, a smattering of photographers, game officials and event security took their familiar places around her as the capacity crowd stood for the flag. The teams, as is now customary, spent that time in their locker rooms. As soon as the lights went back up, the teams returned to the floor to resume their shootarounds. Anyone genuinely invested in the finals would have been unfazed by them briefly stepping away – if they remembered it at all after the Valkyries’ 67-62 win tied the series at two games apiece. But for many watching the game, basketball is beside the point.

Seven years ago, Jay-Z declared that the culture had “moved past kneeling” and similar national anthem protests, seemingly sounding the death knell for an era of sports activism that had helped raise awareness of racial disparities as a broader social movement gathered force. The line cemented his partnership with the NFL as the league bowed to political pressure to crack down on anthem protests, with other major US sports eventually following the NFL’s lead. But rightwing media and politicians never got the memo. They’re still making sports a battleground for patriotism, with basketball as the war’s chief casualty.

Credit OutKick, Fox’s renegade sports arm, for providing the spark that reignited the right’s outrage machine. They tipped off the WNBA finals by making a story out of Atlanta and Golden State leaving the court during the national anthem, then amplified the indignation aimed at LeBron James for appearing to practice his golf swing during the anthem at a Philadelphia 76ers game that same week.

That was all the scene-setting Donald Trump needed. “You know the NFL did that for a while and they stopped because people stopped watching games. I think you should do the same thing with women’s basketball,” Trump said. In a Truth Social post, he called James a “disgrace” and demanded he “apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!”

Basketball has grown accustomed to this kind of punching down from the White House and the familiar cycle of provocation and outrage, especially when the administration’s poll numbers are dragging. James dismissed Trump’s diss as a sign of a “slow news day at the office” and the WNBA declined to engage, beyond noting that players haven’t been on court for the anthem for years now. Meanwhile, the Dream and Valkyries have been too preoccupied with winning their first championship to really enter the chat.

“For me, it’s staying off social media. It’s just going inward with our teammates and staff,” said veteran Golden State center Kiah Stokes, who helped drive her team’s victory with her stout defense of Atlanta star Angel Reese. “Staying together. That’s been one of our keys all season.”

But no matter how hard the WNBA resists the urge to clap back, no matter how valiantly it tries to keep the spotlight on basketball, there will always be someone on the right looking to steal it for their grievance grift. As OutKick and Trump reheated the stale anthem controversy, former NBA player turned Maga wannabe Enes Kanter Freedom was making a grand show of his latest appearance at a WNBA game, asking for special security arrangements so he could watch Game 3 of the finals from a courtside seat. The Dream offered to accommodate Kanter Freedom – who has disrupted WNBA games in the past – with a fully stocked suite, courtesy of the team and State Farm. But Kanter Freedom refused and beat a retreat with his camera crew.

Jennifer Sey, the red-pilled former US gymnastics champion, has attended this year’s finals in her anti-trans athletic gear – and her efforts to incite a reaction from the W’s progressives went largely unnoticed, too.

It is unfortunate that these finals have become a microcosm of the WNBA season, a tug-of-war between a basketball product that has never been better and a political class desperate to bend it to its own agenda. But the longer the right keeps up its fight, the more it gives its game away – exposing the hypocrisy beneath its moral posturing. We’ve seen how urgently conservative culture warriors believe women need protecting when the alleged assailant isn’t transgender. “Cornell’s a fine school,” Trump said in response to the university’s handling of a student’s gang-rape allegations. “I’m sure they’ll do what’s right.” We’ve seen how much this administration cares about its great American heroes as it sends them into an open-ended conflict, keeps sailors at sea for record stretches and downplays casualties, injuries and damage to US assets in the war with Iran – all while slashing veterans’ jobs across the federal government.

We know why basketball makes such a ripe target for attacks from Maga’s crusaders of the American way: the game’s politics lean left, its players are well-traveled, culturally sensitive and have no qualms about dunking on trolls. And we know why the WNBA, in particular, gets under the right’s skin: it is so Black and queer, and its players have set the tone for political protest in American sports. The Dream, specifically, helped usher Raphael Warnock, the Atlanta pastor who delivers sermons from Martin Luther King Jr’s pulpit, into the US Senate.

We see the play Kanter Freedom is trying to run by seeking out an altercation with a player in front of Atlanta’s largely African American crowd, and the statement Sey hopes to make by swanning around queer-friendly Ballhalla in her statementware. We see how closely these grifters actually follow women’s sports. That much was clear again in a recent episode of The Georgia Gang, Atlanta’s long-running political TV roundtable, when the talk turned to the home town team’s WNBA finals berth. “Go Sophie Cunningham, she my’s girl not Angel Reese,” said panelist Phil Kent, a conservative consultant – a contrarian move that also betrayed his refusal to appreciate the absorbing WNBA finals matchup we are being treated to: Maga It girl Cunningham and her Indiana Fever crashed out in the first round. When others at the roundtable praised Reese’s selection as defensive player of the year, Kent doubled down (“I question that”) – and the clip has since drawn a torrent of criticism. “These white men are so broken,” said one Twitter user. “It’s never been about basketball.”

SportsTab.title: Kimi Antonelli seizes F1 US GP pole and chance to seal first world title
SportsTab.text:
Kimi Antonelli claimed pole position for the US Grand Prix with a hugely impressive lap for Mercedes at the Circuit of the Americas. In beating Red Bull’s Max Verstappen into second place, Antonelli did exactly what was required to give him the chance to close out his first world championship title this weekend.

Isack Hadjar did well to secure third for Red Bull, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton in fourth and fifth for Ferrari, and Antonelli’s Mercedes teammate George Russell in sixth.

Antonelli’s first pole since the Belgian GP in July could not have been better timed as he attempts to take his first title. The Italian has a 102-point lead over Russell and needs to be 125 points in front after this race. To take the title he must win on Sunday and have Russell finish outside the top eight, with Hamilton outside the top four. The win certainly looks to be a strong prospect but he still needs his rivals to stumble on Sunday.

He can only do his best and knows that even should the title not be secured here, on this form it will surely be done and dusted by the next round in Mexico.

“We got pole, so we’ll try to win tomorrow,” Antonelli said. “Max has been very quick and did an incredible job in qualifying so it’s not going to be easy. Hopefully we’ll be leading into turn one and we’ll try to set the pace, even though it’s going to be very tight. Very happy with qualifying today, Q3 was very tough with the wind, gusty, unpredictable but happy to stick it on pole.”

It is another striking achievement from the Italian, not least because the Mercedes upgrades applied in Malaysia have made the car more of a handful to drive. Indeed, Russell was a full four-tenths off his teammate, and it was a strong return to form for Antonelli as he looks to become the youngest F1 world champion at just 20 years old.

He was flawless for the lap that proved unbeatable in the Texas sunshine but it was a performance by which Mercedes, too, will be buoyed given they were hoping to extract the maximum from their recent upgrades which had not delivered as expected on their opening salvos in Malaysia and Singapore. With the team having found a way to exploit them, Antonelli gave a reminder of just what a formidable opponent he is.

His engineer, Pete Bonnington, admitted it was somewhat unexpected given both the team’s work on their upgrades and the form of the recently resurgent Red Bull, with Verstappen taking pole and the win at the last two rounds. A sentiment echoed by the beaming Antonelli.

“It was unexpected, we felt it would be close but it was a good surprise,” he said. “I am happy because we have been working very hard on this package and since Singapore we have taken a big step further. The team have done a tremendous job and finally we are seeing the results.”

For the first runs in Q3 in what had been a tightly contested session, with both Red Bull and Ferrari looking to be very much in the mix, it was Antonelli who set the pace. He put in a blistering lap with a time of 1minute 34.035seconds, almost two-tenths up on Verstappen, with the Italian hooking up what was one of his very best laps of the weekend.

On the final runs Verstappen gave his all but could not improve and, although Antonelli too could not go quicker, he had done enough. His time was not bettered and a somewhat unexpected pole was secured with no little style. “Yes man, it’s good to be back,” he said.

For Antonelli, in a season of milestones, including eight wins, his first pole in Austin is his seventh of the season and the first for Mercedes here since Valtteri Bottas last took the top spot in 2019, from which he went on to win – a feat Antonelli will hope to emulate.

The Italian looked very much at his best and has given himself the chance to potentially finish the job. But as Verstappen observed, if not here on Sunday, then at the next round or the round after. The hard yards are over.

TechnologyTab.title: Musk says SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink connection as service restored
TechnologyTab.text:
Elon Muskhas said his company SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink internet service,after Ukrainian officials said connectivity issues appeared to have been resolved.

The tech billionaire accused Ukraine of violating its terms of service by using it for military activity - but denied being responsible for a simultaneous issue with its US-run, military-grade counterpart Starshield.

Kyiv has not officially commented on Musk's latest claim but Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said his post was "very strange".

Musk had earlier denied deliberately throttling Ukraine's connection, which it says hampered its ability to conduct defensive operations for more than a week.

The issue first emerged last week during a broader row between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.

Musk's latest comments, and the seeming restoration of the service, came after US President Donald Trump said he had told the Tesla and X owner to "put it back", having repeatedly denied instructing him to limit the service.

"Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be," Musk wrote on X on Saturday.

"Ukraine['s] military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week."

He went on to say that SpaceX had "done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth" and reiterated his stipulation that Starshield was a different system and controlled by the US government, adding: "What they decide to do is up to them."

He added in a later post: "[Starlink] can be used for infrastructure that is military, but it cannot be used for unequivocally offensive strikes that make it fair game to be struck back."

Reacting to Musk's post, Beskrestnov said that drones operating via Starlink in Ukraine had a speed restriction of 70-90km/h (43-56mph) and did not work on Russian territory.

"Therefore, we physically cannot use commercial Starlink for deep strikes and medium-range strikes," he wrote on Telegram.

"It is very strange that Elon Musk is not aware of Starlink restrictions in Ukraine."

There was no immediate comment from Ukraine's defence ministry.

Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, depending on what communications are needed, both of which run on networks of low Earth orbit satellites launched by SpaceX.

Starlink allows military units to co-ordinate, particularly in remote areas on the battlefield, while Starshield allows Ukrainian drone operators to see targets in real time, as well as operate interceptor drones.

Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles or drones deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work.

Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said earlier on Saturday that the military was now recording a "stable connection", with drones now able to reach speeds in excess of 400km/h. Kyiv previously said the connection would cut out above 161km/h.

"The speeds are now where they need to be," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote on Telegram.

TechnologyTab.title: Are California voters about to impose 'world's first' tax on billionaires?
TechnologyTab.text:
Few places on the planet have as many ultra-wealthy residents as California, a US state known for glamour, coastal mega-mansions, and being home to the rich and famous.

Now voters are about to decide whether the mega-rich among them - including media mogul Oprah Winfrey, Meta head Mark Zuckerberg, Skims cofounder and reality television star Kim Kardashian, and filmmaker George Lucas - should hand over billions of dollars to pay for improvements to healthcare.

Proposition 40 is aimed at levying a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of all of California's billionaires.

There are a little more than 200 such individuals in the state - but that hasn't stopped the measure from dividing leaders and causing some of its ultra-wealthy residents to flee. One billionaire businessman says he's brought jobs to California, but the proposition made him feel "a little bit like I wasn't wanted".

But the vote is also offering regular residents a voice on an issue that has roiled politics for decades.

"I believe this is the first billionaire tax - meaning a wealth tax that is targeting a very extreme percentile of the wealth distribution," says Francesco Trebbi, a public policy professor at the University of California, Berkeley. He noted the measure's historic nature and how it could help even out California's wealth gap.

The state has the largest economy in the country and boasts the fourth largest global economy, bigger than India and the UK. And it is home to one of the highest concentrations of billionaires in the world. But it also has the largest share of homeless people in the nation and one of the highest wealth gaps.

Those who back the measure have argued it helps ensure that the ultra-wealthy are contributing their fair share and will help backfill gaps in the state's budget. The move aims to raise $100bn (£75bn) to make up for federal funding cuts to the state's health-care system.

Suzanne Jimenez, chief of staff for Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West, which helped lead the charge for the initiative, says the measure is a "short-term solution" for massive federal funding cuts coming to California as a result of US President Donald Trump's sweeping tax and spending bill.

"If we do nothing, we're going to see a collapse of our healthcare system, while we figure out a longer-term solution to fund our healthcare," she tells the BBC.

While the ballot measure has many supporters - including some billionaires like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang - it has faced fierce opposition from a variety of figures, from billionaires to the state's liberal governor.

Google co-founder Sergey Brin has given more than $100m to a political organisation funding ballot measures that could block the wealth tax, the Los Angeles Times reports, external.

California Governor Gavin Newsom, whose tenure is coming to an end, is perhaps the most notable political leader opposing it. He has voiced concerns that the measure could cause the wealthy to leave the state and drive out their crucial income tax revenue.

A September poll, external from the Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies and the Los Angeles Times found the proposition has not clearly won over a majority of voters, with 45% of likely voters in favour of the tax, 42% opposed and 13% undecided.

The statewide ballot measure would need to be approved by a majority of residents.

California is not the first place to toy with the idea of taxing the rich. Also on the West Coast, voters in US state of Washington are considering whether to accept or reject a "millionaires tax" - a 9.9% tax on income over $1m a year.

While wealth taxes were once a fairly common form of taxation in Europe, they have rapidly fallen out of favour and now only exist in three European countries – Spain, Norway and Switzerland, says Dr Kristian Niemietz, head of political economy at the Institute of Economic Affairs.

Niemietz believes wealth taxes are "more trouble than they are worth" because they cause administrative issues, suppress investment, lead to capital flight and, in the end, do not raise much revenue.

In the case of Norway, a local news organisation found that an increase in the wealth tax led to more super wealthy people leaving the country in 2022, external than in the preceding 13 years combined. A study on Switzerland, external found that a 0.1 percentage point increase in a wealth tax reduced taxable wealth by 3.5%.

The California measure, if approved, would apply retroactively to those with a net worth of at least $1bn who resided in California as of 1 January 2026. At least six of the state's 200 plus billionaires have reportedly left California ahead of that deadline to avoid the tax.

They include Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, venture capitalist Peter Thiel, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick and Hankey Group founder Don Hankey.

Hankey, a Los Angeles billionaire who has lived in California all his life, told Forbes he left for the state of Nevada as a result of the proposed wealth tax.

"I think we've created a lot of jobs in California. We have a few thousand people working for us and we have a profit sharing plan. And I have to leave the state," he said, adding that the measure made him feel like he wasn't "wanted" in the state.

Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg told the company's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California over the proposed tax.

To prevent him from leaving the state - where the company is headquartered - Meta agreed to a new stock deal that gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn, even more shares in the company to make up for the billions he would lose if the measure passes in November. Estimates say he could owe as much as $12.5bn.

DoorDash cofounder Andy Fang, who has an estimated net worth of $1.6bn, has called the measure "stupid" and wrote on X that "proposals like this make it irresponsible for me not to plan leaving the state".

Income inequality in the US is at some of its highest levels, external in over three decades, with the top 1% of households owning nearly 32% of all US wealth in the third quarter of 2025. It is also near historic highs in California.

Economic inequality is a concern among most Californians, with 72% believing that the gap between the rich and poor is widening and a similar share holding that state government should do more to reduce the gap, according to a statewide survey, external from the Public Policy Institute of California.

Trebbi says it is an "anti-elite, anti-system sentiment" driving the policy.

"This is really not about Prop 40," he says, but rather about trying to "re-balance the scale a little bit".

TechnologyTab.title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI
TechnologyTab.text:
Mohammed Ashim has been cutting hair and trimming beards for four years in Bengaluru.

But recently the 22-year old has been strapping a camera to his head to record his work.

The camera only records his hands and fingers - his client's faces are blurred out.

"The routine is simple, but you have to be disciplined about how you move. The operations team taught me that my hands always have to stay cleanly inside the frame, the lighting has to be sharp, and I can't tilt my head too abruptly while working."

He wears the camera for five or six hours a day.

"It's good money, but honestly, the feeling of doing something this futuristic is what keeps me excited. I never imagined my razor techniques would be useful to a global tech company," says Ashim.

He is one of hundreds of thousands of workers across the world paid to record their activities.

Ashim's footage is collected by a local company, which might have hundreds of people filming their work.

That video is then sold on to technology companies and research organisations who use it to train artificial intelligence - in particular so-called physical AI, a type of artificial intelligence that can control robots in the real world.

Rashdan Technologies collects and processes such human generated data.

"Every robotics company, every frontier AI lab, has a specific kind of data they want: industrial tasks, agriculture, household chores, small business work like pottery, garment-making, embroidery, candle-making. We go wherever the task is," says co-founder and CEO Shahil Baig.

His company pays $5 to $10 (£3.74; £7.47) for eight to 10 hours of recorded work.

"For a lot of these people, that's meaningful," Baig says.

Making sure workers give their consent and are comfortable with the process is important, he says.

"We record hands, not faces, and where multi-camera rigs do capture more of the body or environment, we blur faces out. No names, no contact details, nothing that identifies them personally goes into what we hand off."

But his customers are getting more demanding.

"Now clients are asking for four to six cameras rigged around a person's head to cover the entire scene, not just the hands.

"Getting someone to agree to one small camera is one conversation. Getting them to agree to wearing what's effectively a five-camera headset is a completely different, and harder, one. We pay more for that tier of data collection because of what we're asking of people."

And the industry is becoming more crowded, Agarwal expects dozens more competitors to emerge in India this year.

Why is such data so important?

If you want robots to navigate the real world, they can't just be trained inside computer simulations, argues Manish Agarwal, the founder of Humyn Labs, which collects and processes human-generated data.

Most of that data comes from video, but sometimes collectors wear hardware on their hands and fingers to capture physical contact.

"Physical tasks require high-quality signals involving limb movements, fingers, wrists, elbows, shoulders and dynamic force application. For example: applying the correct grip force so a plastic bottle doesn't crumble versus a steel glass," he says.

And until recently, that data was not available.

"There is no existing internet archive of embodied human activity - no dataset of a kitchen being cleaned, or a car being assembled by hands that know exactly how much force to apply. That data has to be captured from scratch, in the real world, across diverse environments," says Agarwal, whose company has bases in Bangalore and San Francisco.

At the moment his firm has 96,000 data collectors across countries in Latin America and Southeast Asia.

Humyn Labs filters the thousands of hours of video supplied by those collectors, selecting the most useful content. It's then labelled so the AI knows what it is looking at and packaged in a format that can be used by clients.

"You need to source across a variety of factories, a variety of tasks, in different geographies because if you want to build deployment for US factories or US houses, you'd want environments that are a proxy for that. Residential houses in India may not be the right context for building a robotics use case for the US."

TechnologyTab.title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab
TechnologyTab.text:
The UK says it will establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL) to help strengthen its defences against emerging biological threats.

As part of Wednesday's Budget, the government will commit £100m to establishing the new, "world first" institute with the support of leading AI firms.

The chancellor will also pledge millions of pounds in spending across a range of initiatives aimed at shoring up the UK's ability to respond to evolving cyber, biological and AI-enabled threats.

"AI will transform daily life: every firm, community, hospital, school, and every aspect of our economy can benefit," John Healey said.

"I understand and share the concerns of working people, so I am setting out a distinctively British approach to AI.

"One that doesn't leave workers behind and defends our national interest, while ensuring the benefits of AI-enabled growth are felt right across the country."

The full details about the role and remit of the new lab are yet to emerge.

But the AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said it would be a "major new global institution" that brings together "world-leading scientific expertise" to ensure the UK can safeguard its citizens and goals as AI develops.

"That means staying ahead of emerging threats, from cyber attacks to biological risks, while building more of the critical technology our security depends on," he said.

"By backing British science, advanced chips and our own AI companies, we can strengthen our national security, rebuild Britain's industrial strength and create good, skilled jobs across the country."

The AI Biosecurity Lab's creation will also be supported by leading AI developers, with OpenAI and Anthropic providing £200m worth of AI model credits that can be spent on the use of their models.

TechnologyTab.title: Civil servant who juggled five jobs says he was 'surprised' to be charged with fraud
TechnologyTab.text:
A civil servant accused of fraudulently juggling multiple government jobs says he was ''surprised'' to have been charged with fraud.

Kashim Chowdhury told the jury at Southwark Crown Court he had not been dishonest in failing to tell his employers he had other government jobs.

"At that time I was just on auto pilot, I was like a robot, I was not thinking clearly," he said.

Chowdhury, 55, from east London, is accused of nine counts of fraud. He denies acting dishonestly or intending to make a dishonest gain.

Between 2020 and 2023 Chowdhury had eight overlapping public sector jobs. He was contractually obliged to work full time and was paid a full-time salary by each organisation. He is accused of fraudulently earning more than £284,000.

In March 2023 Chowdhury began working for the Home Office despite being under contract to work full time at the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade and the Food Standards Agency.

The court was told he started the Home Office job while on sick leave from three of his other jobs.

Prosecuting barrister Lucy Organ asked him: "If you were really sick for work, how were you able to start your work at the Home Office?"

Chowdhury said: "I did not want this job at the Home Office, I was told there would be adequate support and I could work whatever hours I wanted to work."

Organ also asked why he did not submit a sick note to the Home Office "You were using these sick notes to be able to cope. It was all too much wasn't it?"

Chowdhury rejected the suggestion, adding: "I wanted to carry on working."

In May 2023, Chowdhury was contracted to work 183 hours a week, more than the number of hours in seven days.

He told the jury he agreed with his employers to work flexibly and that his work was project or output based. He said this was agreed "informally" via text messages but the phones used to send the texts had gone missing when his house was searched by investigators.

He said that to cope with the workload he would work from 07:00 on Saturdays and Sundays and not finish until 20:00 or 21:00.

Organ asked him: "Wasn't that a bit much for you?"

"I was house bound, I was looking after my mum," he said.

The prosecution alleges Chowdhury managed to keep his overlapping jobs secret because he worked entirely remotely. He told his employers he was the sole carer for his elderly mother and the prosecution alleges he "exploited this opportunity".

His line manager at the UKHSA, Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023 to discuss his sick leave.

She previously told the court she was surprised when he logged on wearing white make-up because his name led her to expect to see an Asian man with darker skin.

She told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck."

But Chowdhury denied having worn make-up at the meeting

''That's a smear, I've never worn make-up in my life. At that particular time, I was suffering from anxiety and depression. I had already submitted my sick note, there was no need to put on make-up.''

The trial continues.

TechnologyTab.title: PHP: What is it and why did it spark a global cyber security scramble?
TechnologyTab.text:
For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in the technology underpinning much of the internet.

It took AI to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert.

Researchers who helped surface the vulnerabilities in PHP - a popular server-side programming language used in web development for decades - warned platforms which use it could be exposed to potential hacks.

Governments and cyber-security agencies rushed to contain the fallout, urging website owners to check if their sites were affected and, if so, install updates to patch the issue or consider going offline.

There have been no reports of any successful exploits of the flaw, coined php2shell, so far.

But in the days since the issues came to light, disruption to sites and services has continued to ripple around the world.

Most people may not have heard of PHP, but they probably interact with it daily.

It stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, an open-source, back-end programming language which runs on a web server.

Developed in the early 1990s to help serve dynamic web pages and applications, PHP still powers lots of platforms today, including Wikipedia, online shops and WordPress – the system behind many websites.

When you visit a site, PHP is the code which collects data and effectively turns it into a page you can read.

It has also been used to write a number of tools for building or speeding up the creation of web apps, with Laravel, Symfony and Drupal among popular PHP frameworks.

According to cyber-security firm Wiz, which helped uncover the critical PHP vulnerabilities surfaced this week, PHP powers 70% of the world's websites.

It is maintained by a non-profit called the PHP Foundation, external, composed of individuals and companies which depend on the language and aim to ensure its "long-term prosperity".

A group of cyber-security researchers and organisations disclosed two vulnerabilities within PHP this week, which they warned could have the potential to upend sites across the internet.

Cyber firms Wiz and Calif said the flaws were inherent in the language itself, affecting versions of PHP released over the last decade.

The technical bugs, given the technical IDs CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, were ranked a 9.2 out of 10 in severity by researchers.

Calif researcher Ryan Austin, who helped uncover it, told the BBC it was "the most serious vulnerability I've ever found".

Wiz wrote in a blog post, external about its findings that, under the right conditions, hackers could exploit the bugs to take control of affected web servers and steal sensitive data - saying everything built on PHP was left exposed.

AI could also make such attacks easier and faster, Paul Spain, chief executive of Gorilla Cyber Security, told the BBC.

He estimated the flaw could affect "millions and millions" of websites.

Jill Slay, a cyber-security researcher at the University of Adelaide, said it would be "disastrous" if hackers or countries weaponised the flaw and seized private data from websites.

The alert on 21 October disrupted services globally, from gaming platforms to government portals and online forums.

It included Wikimedia - the organisation behind the online encyclopaedia Wikipedia - which took down a number of its systems as a precautionary measure.

Sites and pages were also taken offline by the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and some BBC pages, with the Netherlands' cyber-security agency also pulling its website on Wednesday.

But while many sites were back up by Thursday, others were still being taken down temporarily elsewhere as people and businesses check for potential exposure.

The UK Government revealed on Thursday some "limited" services may be offline temporarily.

It said 32 sites had been taken down as a precaution, none of them large public-facing services.

In France, telecommunications company Orange also said it had suspended access to certain services globally while it deployed security fixes.

On Friday, local media in Japan reported telecom operator SoftBank Corp had temporarily suspended emergency alerts for earthquakes, tsunamis and other disasters.

According to the Mainichi newspaper, external, SoftBank customers have been urged to make sure they have other ways to get alerts about natural disasters - with its mobile phone alerts not set to sound even in the event of a strong earthquake.

The service is reportedly set to resume on Monday.

Some experts warn the issue could leave poorly maintained websites, particularly those belonging to smaller organisations with limited security resources, at greater risk.

More attempts to exploit these flaws are likely in the coming weeks since the technical details are now being made public, said cyber-security researcher Salil Kanhere of UNSW Sydney.

The PHP Foundation rolled out patches on Wednesday to fix the vulnerabilities that had been lurking in their software for years.

"All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately," the company said.

Authorities and security organisations around the world have echoed those warnings to website operators to secure their platforms.

The US National Security Agency told all organisations, external that use PHP to take their systems offline if they were unable to patch them immediately, adding that the flaw could provide a "direct path" to exploit a system's database.

"These risks are serious enough to require immediate patching across United States Government departments and agencies," the agency said.

Its counterparts in the EU, Singapore and Australia have also issued similar alerts.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP in posts on X.

Tech companies also sought to quickly secure their systems.

E-commerce giant Amazon said it was targeted in multiple attempts days before the public disclosure of the PHP issue, but its websites were operating as normal.

Matthew Prince, the boss of internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, also said it had seen "thousands" of attempts to exploit the PHP vulnerabilities across its network in the 10 hours before it was publicly announced.

"That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions now," he wrote on X, external.

As of Friday morning, no successful attacks had been reported.

But experts have warned any impact may take time to become fully apparent.

And operators of a number of services where PHP may have been used - not just in web development - are still being urged to check their systems and implement updates, where necessary.

"It is important to remember that PHP is not limited to web applications," said Daniel Stewart, head of threat intelligence at global risk manager LRQA.

"It is commonly found in the management interfaces of network appliances, load balancers, and embedded devices, which are often overlooked during these incidents."

According to some cyber-security researchers using scans to check servers at risk of the PHP vulnerability, the rate of organisations implementing patches has climbed - but not as quickly as might be hoped globally.

The issue affects back-end website and web development processes that will be invisible to many users - meaning most people won't need to take any action.

But small businesses with sites, including those built using WordPress, may be wondering how to protect themselves.

Those who own websites or manage infrastructure running PHP have been urged to secure their websites by updating to the latest version.

Ethical hacker Ken Munro, who has spent years finding security flaws in computer systems, says installing the fixes - known as patching - is "a bit like running a Windows update".

If a hosting company or web developer manages your website, contact them and ask whether the PHP security fixes have been applied - something that must be applied to PHP itself and cannot be resolved by updating WordPress or its plugins.

If you look after your website yourself, Munro says "it is your own responsibility to make sure fixes are applied".

The UK's National Cyber Security Centre recommends, external considering temporarily taking sites offline if updates or temporary protections cannot be applied quickly enough.

The US National Security Agency has also urged "heightened awareness" in the coming weeks, telling people to closely monitor updates from software vendors.

"Vigilance in applying patches related to those systems is paramount," it said.

And while the onus lies mainly on website operators, users should stay alert for any security advice issued by affected services, such as requests to change passwords, Kanhere said.

He warned people to be alert to any phishing messages exploiting the publicity around the incident too.

TechnologyTab.title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber security scramble
TechnologyTab.text:
Microsoft boss Satya Nadella says he has not seen anything like the PHP emergency "in a long, long time".

Referencing the ongoing global efforts to fix the critical cyber-security flaw in millions of websites, he told a conference "it was a long day and a long night, I know, for all the IT and security folks".

Other IT and cyber experts have told the BBC about their struggles in the last 48 hours, whose stories give us an insight into what it is like at the coalface of a major cyber emergency. But also highlight how misinformation and panic has made things a lot worse.

"It's been relentless," says UK-based system administrator Adam Mudd.

He said he had never had so many messages from people who were worried about their websites.

"The biggest challenge has been juggling clients who want their sites taken offline as a precaution, while trying to coordinate updates and fixes across countless different setups," he said.

"Sometimes it takes me longer to take a website down than to fix the PHP problem."

PHP is a very popular programming language which powers millions of websites.

But two critical flaws were found with the system that led to the emergency response, with national cyber-security authorities urging IT teams to download a security fix urgently or take websites and servers offline.

Mudd says since then he has been under enormous pressure and has lost a huge amount of sleep - working early and not finishing until 22:30 BST to secure his customers' systems.

In Mauritius, IT administrator Loganaden Velvindron said he too was flat out since his team realised just how much software relies on PHP.

"Many versions of php running are completely end-of-life, so we are having to rebuilding web apps and change code in some cases," he said.

He said part of the problem was the announcement about the security vulnerabilities in PHP came as a surprise, without much time to prepare for action.

Jon Jones, Technical director for a digital advertising company, was also spurred into action by the alerts.

"Seeing the warning drop was definitely eye-opening and a new experience we've not dealt with before," he said.

"But, in a way, it was exciting feeling like a bit of a Hollywood action scene."

The PHP Foundation, which manages the programming language, released its software fix and there was a scramble for people to download it.

Jones said it felt like "the race was on" when the patch launched at 15:00 BST on Wednesday.

"It was also a bit nerve-racking as anyone who has applied software updates before would know, there's always a chance than an update can cause other issues," he said.

The rush came as someone had leaked details of the PHP flaw early - and it was heavily rumoured that cyber-criminals were already trying to carry out attacks.

But cyber experts are also now questioning whether or not those rumours were real.

"We were flooded with rubbish intel about hackers being out there actively with working Proof of Concept (PoC) methods," said UK cyber expert Daniel Card.

He said he also been flat out since Tuesday when the rumours of PHP hacks began circulating.

"This isn't the first time we've had a situation like this but it feels like it's been on another dimension," he said.

He agreed that on paper the PHP vulnerabilities were very serious and should be taken seriously, but he and many others are frustrated with the misinformation about hackers being on the loose.

As well as the alerts from government agencies - even the Prime Minister of Japan - cyber-security companies also made errors which didn't help.

One major firm in this space issued warnings saying hackers had a working PoC - only to have to retract it.

In spite of warnings from Cloudflare and AWS that "millions of hacking attempts" had been made every hour, there is also no evidence of large scale data breaches or cyber-attacks.

It is true that hackers have been seen to use AI to attempt to build attack methods, but none of them seem to be working at scale at the moment - something that may well change soon.

AI was also used to find the PHP flaws which had been hidden from human researchers for decades.

The IT workers we spoke to all agreed that these kinds of serious flaws were going to be uncovered more frequently now that AI tools had become so good at hacking.

But some in the industry are concerned about how people were told about the critical vulnerabilities in PHP, as they fear improvements in AI will throw up more incidents like it.

"We're going to find scary vulnerabilities with the amazing capabilities that OpenAI and Anthropic are bringing online, but we need to calibrate the messaging," posted Mark Maunder, founder of Wordfence - a Wordpress security tool.

He said there was a risk of "alert fatigue" which could be a big problem if a fully exploitable and serious vulnerability arose.

TechnologyTab.title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax
TechnologyTab.text:
Meta has agreed to a new deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to prevent him from leaving California over a proposed state tax on billionaires.

The agreement gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn (£149bn), even more shares in Meta to make up for the fraction of his fortune he may lose if the tax wins voter approval in November.

The measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on residents with a net worth of more than $1bn. It would likely see the Facebook co-founder pay around $10bn in additional state taxes.

He secured the deal with a special committee of Meta after "robust" and "at several points, contentious" negotiations, according to a Wednesday financial disclosure.

California is home to most of the US's technology giants and there are around 225 billionaires who reside in the state, according to the Americans for Tax Fairness campaign group.

The wealth of such people, including Zuckerberg, has ballooned in recent years. Meanwhile, his estimated effective tax rate in California was less than 1%, external each year.

Nevertheless, Zuckerberg told Meta's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California, and even selling his property in the state. His main homes in Californa are in Palo Alto and Lake Tahoe.

Such a move "would be public and inevitably noted and commented upon by company employees", Zuckerberg told the board.

It would also "raise questions for management of the company going forward", he claimed.

In response, Meta decided to create more shares of stock in the company in order to give Zuckerberg a way to essentially make up any wealth he may lose through the tax proposal.

Through what's known as a stock split announced by the company on Wednesday, Meta created an entirely new type of stock and gave one new share to each existing shareholder. Zuckerberg is one of the company's largest shareholders and famously controls the company through the design of his holdings.

Through the deal, he will receive more stock, more often, and also be able to sell it on a quarterly basis, according to the company's financial filing. The shares will not change his level control over Meta, but they will allow him to cash in more easily on the company's value.

The deal appears to be effective even if the one-time tax in California does not pass, and will go on for eight years - as long as Zuckerberg remains a resident of California.

Meta called the deal with Zuckerberg its "Founder Alignment Agreement," saying it was "critically important" to keep him leading the company from California given the "dramatic and unprecedented transformation taking place in the tech industry and global economy related to artificial intelligence."

The company alluded to problems the company experienced during the Covid-19 pandemic, when Zuckerberg began working outside of the office and mostly from his large compound in Kauai, Hawaii.

After a surge in hiring at Meta during the pandemic, a whistleblower scandal that led to renewed focus on child safety, and a refocus within the company to building out the "metaverse," which included renaming the company Meta from Facebook, the company began mass layoffs and restructuring.

Layoffs have continued into this year. The company's headcount is down 15% from a year ago, meaning it has shed at least 10,000 workers.

Today, the company has moved away from the "metaverse," or virtual platforms, and is more focused on artificial intelligence products and related tools.

With Zuckerberg leading the company's efforts to catch up in the AI race, Meta's board said it sees a future of "tremendous market opportunity" for the company.

Major tech companies are set to spend an estimated $1 trillion, external this year alone developing AI and the costly infrastructure around it, like data centres.

Meta said on Wednesday it planned to spend as much as $145bn this year on AI projects. The company has increased the amount it expects to spend on AI each financial quarter so far this year.

It is spending so much on the technology that it posted negative cash flow for the first time since the company went public 14 years ago. Cash flow represents the money a company retains after paying for operations and investments, meaning Meta is now spending more money than it is bringing in.

And the company intends to spend even more in the year ahead. Susan Li, Meta's chief financial officer, said on Wednesday that another benefit of the stock split would be to give the company more ways to finance future spending on AI work.

The degree of the company's spending on AI, without an clear new revenue stream coming from it, appeared to spook investors on Thursday.

Meta's shares fell more than 7%, wiping more than $100bn off of the company's market capitalisation, a key metric used worldwide to measure the value of a publicly-traded company.

TechnologyTab.title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found
TechnologyTab.text:
Organisations and businesses are still scrambling to update their systems after cyber-security flaws were revealed in a widely-used programming language, PHP.

Websites around the world were taken offline on Wednesday and Thursday after the developers of PHP said "critical vulnerabilities" were found in the back-end language, used in web development for decades.

Researchers warned the "severe" flaws could expose millions of sites using it to potential hacks if left unpatched - and the UK government was among those to take some sites offline as a precaution.

There have been no successful attacks reported so far, but experts say any impact may take time - even months - to become fully apparent.

Downing Street said on Thursday "some" limited government services "may be offline" while security work was being carried out.

"The information I have is that 32 Government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable," tech minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra told the House of Lords.

She attributed this to having "largely resulted from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied".

The government did not specify which services were taken offline - but it said no large UK public-facing critical services had been affected.

A spokesperson said work had already taken place across government to "identify and fix potential exposures to our systems and our experts are continuing to work closely with both OpenAI and international partners on this issue".

"But this does not mean they were hacked, and work continues to resolve any issues," they added.

Olly Whitehouse, chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), called the event "unprecedented".

"It will be universally felt, I suspect," he told BBC Radio 4's World At One.

But he said there were "no indications" of any successful breaches by hackers.

He said the NCSC was "starting to see positive confirmation" that advice sent to those affected, external had been received and was being acted on.

Cyber-security lecturer Rory Hopcraft told the BBC the government needed to make sure that its own infrastructure was up-to-date.

"Hacking has been around for many years," he said.

"The government are the ones who set the rules for other organisations... they just need to effectively be practising what they're preaching at this point."

Dean Presley, who has a garage in Chepstow, South Wales, told BBC Your Voice he had been unable to properly process MOTs online.

He said his computer system had been down since Wednesday morning, and while he has experienced outages before, they have not lasted this long.

"MOTs can be conducted and they're legal but none of the paperwork and certificates can be printed and they're not on the system," Dean said.

He said this has forced him to write everything on paper documents, leading to delays for customers.

PHP stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor.

It's a programming language which runs on a web server, behind the scenes of a website, and effectively lets you see the sites you visit.

When you go to a site, PHP is the code which collects data and effectively turns it into a page you can read.

It was developed in the early 1990s to help serve dynamic web pages and applications, but still powers lots of platforms today.

PHP has been used across a wide range of platforms including Wikipedia, online shops and WordPress – the system behind many websites - as well as to write tools to build web apps, with Laravel, Symfony and Drupal among popular PHP frameworks.

According to cyber-security firm Wiz, external, which helped uncover the critical PHP vulnerabilities surfaced this week, PHP powers 70% of the world's websites.

And it said the flaws - now coined "php2shell" - were inherent in the language itself, affecting many past versions of it.

The PHP Foundation, the non-profit which maintains the programming language, warned this meant that, under the right conditions, an unauthenticated attacker would be able to remotely execute code on servers running PHP.

Some large organisations said they had seen a high volume of attempts to breach their systems.

Matthew Prince, the boss of internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, wrote on X, external on Thursday that the company saw "thousands" of attempts to exploit the PHP vulnerabilities across its network in the 10 hours before it was publicly announced.

"That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions now," he added.

Amazon also says it saw hackers attempt to exploit the flaws, but its websites were operating as normal.

While the impact of the PHP flaw remains to be seen, disruption continued for businesses and organisations after many sites were taken down on Wednesday.

The website of a Dutch agency specialising in cyber-security, Finland's government and parts of Wikipedia, taken temporarily offline, had returned to business as usual by Thursday.

But a number of sites appeared to have been taken offline on Thursday, as operators rushed to check if PHP might be running within their systems or if any patches were required.

In France, telecommunications company Orange also said, external it had suspended access to certain services globally while it deployed security fixes.

According to some cyber-security researchers using scans to check servers at risk of the PHP vulnerability, the rate of organisations implementing patches - but not as quickly as might be hoped globally.

"The window to respond has shrunk dramatically," said Matt Hull, VP of cyber intelligence and response at global cyber security company NCC Group.

"A few years ago, attackers might have taken weeks to exploit a vulnerability. Now, it can be days or hours."

Hull also highlighted the extent of the task facing developers and engineers working to deal with the issue.

"Several days into this incident, security professionals might already be dealing with significant burnout," he said, urging a need to "make time to rest, share the workload and look after each other".

"Resilience depends on people as much as technology."
